name: TL331IDBVR
title: Single voltage comparator, open-collector output, 2 V to 36 V supply (TL331, TL331K, TL331B, TL391B)
summary: One voltage comparator in a 5-pin SOT-23, with a PNP Darlington input stage whose common-mode range reaches ground and an NPN open-collector output that only sinks current. It runs from 2 V to 36 V on one supply, or from split supplies whose difference is 2 V to 36 V. TL331 (I grade, -40 °C to 85 °C) and TL331K (-40 °C to 105 °C) are the original device; TL331B is a newer, pin-compatible version with lower offset, bias and supply current, 38 V ratings and 2 kV HBM ESD over -40 °C to 125 °C, and TL391B is the B version with its inputs and output on other pins. TL331IDBVR is the TL331 I grade on a 3000-piece reel.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The comparator checks an input of 0 V to 30 V on IN- against a reference Vref on IN+. VCC is 5 V and GND is ground. The open-collector output is pulled up to 5 V by RPULLUP, so it reads high while the input is below Vref and is pulled low once the input rises above it. The design example uses Vref = 2.5 V, 100 mV of overdrive and a 15 pF load.

parts.note: Output pull-up; sized for VLOGIC/RPULLUP of 1 µA to 4 mA.

notes: The supply and the pull-up are both 5 V; the pull-up may sit on a separate logic supply of 2 V to 36 V.

circuits.title: Layout example: supply bypassing
circuits.description: Supply decoupling around the SOT-23 part. A 0.1 µF capacitor goes from VCC to ground right at the pin. When the part runs on split supplies, GND is the negative rail and a second 0.1 µF capacitor goes from it to ground; on a single supply GND is ground itself and that capacitor is left off.

operation.text: TL331 comes in an I grade (-40 °C to 85 °C) and a K grade (-40 °C to 105 °C). TL331B is built on a newer process with lower offset, bias and supply currents, faster response and a -40 °C to 125 °C range, and replaces either TL331 grade pin for pin. TL391B is the same B device with OUT on pin 1, IN- on pin 3 and IN+ on pin 4. Both pinouts have their inputs swapped relative to a similar, common SOT-23 comparator pinout.

The inputs are a PNP Darlington pair, which gives high gain, fast response and small bias current, and sets the common-mode limit: comparisons are accurate with the inputs between ground and VCC - 1.5 V. Later silicon adds a clamp around one input transistor so that inputs above the common-mode range behave as the original part did. The differential input may be as large as the supply rating, ±36 V (±38 V for the B versions).

The output is the collector of an NPN transistor whose emitter is GND. It conducts when IN- is above IN+ by more than the offset, and is off (high impedance, high through a pull-up) otherwise. Low-level output voltage rises roughly in proportion to the sink current. Outputs of several parts can be tied together to form a wired-AND, and the output suits TTL, MOS and CMOS inputs.

operation.topic: Inputs inside and outside the common-mode range
operation.text: With both inputs inside 0 V to VCC - 1.5 V the output follows their difference. If IN- is above the range and IN+ inside it, the output is low and sinking. If IN+ is above the range and IN- inside it, the output is off. With both inputs above the range the behaviour is covered by application note SNOAA35.

A single supply of 2 V to 36 V, or split supplies, both work; on split supplies the total between them must stay within 2 V to 36 V and VCC must be at least 1.5 V above the input common-mode voltage. Supply current hardly changes with supply voltage.

Overdrive is how far the differential input goes past the offset voltage; it must exceed VIO for a correct decision. More overdrive gives a shorter response time. The output rises at a rate set by the pull-up resistor and load capacitance, and falls at a rate set by the output transistor's resistance and the load capacitance; heavier output current also affects the edge.

A design starts from the input voltage range, the smallest overdrive to be resolved, the output current and pull-up voltage, and the response time needed. The pull-up supply may be 2 V to 36 V, and the wide supply range lets the part shift a logic level up or down.
The B versions have dedicated ESD protection on every pin; their HBM rating is 2 kV, against 1 kV for TL331.

Noise on VCC eats into the upper end of the common-mode range and can cause wrong comparisons, especially with fast, noisy or AC inputs and no hysteresis. Put a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor from VCC to ground, and another from the negative rail to ground when one is used. On a single supply, no capacitor goes between the GND pin and system ground.
A short from the output to ground may last indefinitely; a short from the output to VCC can overheat and destroy the part.
